NO negative marking for MSQ or NAT questions.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to complete the sentence:
"Despite ______ opposition from the board, the proposal was passed unanimously."
questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• "Despite" signals a contrast: strong opposition, yet a unanimous pass. "Vehement" (forceful, intense) supplies the necessary contrast; the weaker options do not.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) "Tacit" means unspoken/implied — too weak to justify "despite" against a unanimous outcome.
(B) Correct — supplies the necessary contrast with "unanimously".
(C) Negligible opposition would not need "despite" to explain a unanimous pass.
(D) Imaginary opposition is not real opposition at all, making "despite" nonsensical.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution:
Answer: C
Explanation:
• The correct spelling is "Maintenance" — note the "e" after "Maint" and before "nance".
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Incorrectly inserts "ai" in the second syllable.
(B) Incorrectly uses "e" where "a" is needed in the final syllable.
(C) Correct.
(D) Incorrectly uses "a" instead of "e" in the second syllable.

questions.question: Select the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to "TRANSIENT".
questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• "Transient" means lasting only a short time. Its direct opposite is "permanent" (lasting indefinitely).
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) A near-synonym of transient, not an antonym.
(B) Correct.
(C) Describes rapid change, not duration — a different axis of meaning.
(D) A near-synonym of transient, not an antonym.

questions.question:
Wheat yield (q/ha) recorded across 5 trial plots is: 42, 38, 45, 40, 50.
Find the median yield.
questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• Sorted: 38, 40, 42, 45, 50. The middle (3rd of 5) value is 42 q/ha.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) This is the second-lowest value, not the median.
(B) Correct — the middle value of the sorted list.
(C) This is the second-highest value, not the median.
(D) This equals the mean, not the median, of the data set.

questions.question: Given: "All combine harvesters are self-propelled machines" and "Some self-propelled machines are tractors." Which conclusion necessarily follows?

options.C: No combine harvester is a tractor
options.D: None of the above conclusions necessarily follows

questions.solution:
Answer: D
Explanation:
• The "self-propelled machines" that are tractors need not be the same subset as combine harvesters — this is the classic undistributed-middle-term case. No valid conclusion about combine harvesters and tractors can be drawn from these two premises alone.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Overreaches — not supported by the premises.
(B) Not guaranteed — the "some" self-propelled machines that are tractors may be entirely disjoint from combine harvesters.
(C) Not guaranteed either — the premises do not rule out overlap.
(D) Correct — the syllogism has an undistributed middle term, so no conclusion follows validly.

questions.question: A cooperative loan of ₹5,00,000 is taken at 10% p.a., compounded annually. Find the total amount payable after 2 years.
questions.solution:
Answer: C
Explanation:
• Amount = P(1+r)ⁿ = 5,00,000 × (1.10)² = 5,00,000 × 1.21 = ₹6,05,000.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Results from using simple interest (10%×2yr = 20%) instead of compounding.
(B) An intermediate rounding, not the compounded value.
(C) Correct.
(D) Overestimates the compounded value.

questions.question: Harvester A alone can harvest a field in 10 hours; harvester B alone in 15 hours. They work together, but A stops working 3 hours before the field is fully harvested (B works the entire time, A leaves early). Find the total time taken to harvest the field.
questions.solution:
Answer: C
Explanation:
• Let total time = T hours. A works (T−3) h, B works T h.
• Work done: (T−3)/10 + T/15 = 1. Multiplying by 30: 3(T−3) + 2T = 30 ⟹ 5T = 39 ⟹ T = 7.8 h.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Not consistent with correctly setting up the work-equation with the 3 h early departure.
(B) Does not satisfy the work equation when substituted back.
(C) Correct.
(D) Overestimates — inconsistent with the combined-rate equation.

questions.question: A field requires 120 kg N/ha and 60 kg K₂O/ha, to be supplied using only urea (46% N) and MOP (60% K₂O) — MOP first to meet all the K₂O, and urea to supply all the N. Find the total mass of fertilizer applied (kg/ha), to the nearest kg.
questions.solution:
Answer: C
Explanation:
• MOP needed for K₂O: 60 ÷ 0.60 = 100 kg/ha (contributes no N).
• Urea needed for N: 120 ÷ 0.46 = 260.9 kg/ha.
• Total fertilizer = 100 + 260.9 ≈ 361 kg/ha.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Underestimates the urea requirement.
(B) Still an underestimate of the correctly computed total.
(C) Correct.
(D) Overestimates the total.

questions.question:
[Figure description: A square sheet of paper is folded in half twice, each fold parallel to a side of the sheet, producing a smaller square of 4 layers. A small triangular corner (away from both fold lines) is then cut off.]
When the sheet is fully unfolded, how many holes appear in it?
questions.solution:
Answer: C
Explanation:
• Each fold doubles the number of paper layers; two folds give 4 layers. A cut through all 4 layers at a corner away from the fold lines reproduces the cut at that corresponding corner in each of the 4 unfolded quadrants, giving 4 holes.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Correct only for an unfolded (single-layer) sheet — not the case here.
(B) Would correspond to only one fold, not two.
(C) Correct — 2 folds ⟹ 4 layers ⟹ 4 holes.
(D) Would require 3 folds (8 layers), not 2.

questions.question: In a survey of 150 farmers: 80 use certified seed, 65 use bio-fertilizer, and 30 use both. How many farmers use neither?
questions.solution:
Answer: C
Explanation:
• Using certified seed or bio-fertilizer = 80 + 65 − 30 = 115.
• Using neither = 150 − 115 = 35.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Results from an arithmetic slip in the union total.
(B) Coincides with the "both" count, not the correct "neither" figure.
(C) Correct.
(D) Results from omitting the overlap term when computing the union.

questions.question: Evaluate: lim(x→0) [ (1 − cos 2x) / x² ]
questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• Using 1 − cos θ ≈ θ²/2 for small θ, with θ = 2x: 1 − cos 2x ≈ (2x)²/2 = 2x².
• Limit of (2x²)/x² = 2.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Results from omitting the factor of 4 from (2x)² before halving.
(B) Correct.
(C) Results from omitting the 1/2 factor in the small-angle approximation.
(D) Results from wrongly assuming the limit is trivially zero.

questions.question: For the diagonal matrix A = [[3, 0], [0, 5]], the sum of its eigenvalues equals:
questions.solution:
Answer: A
Explanation:
• For a diagonal matrix, the eigenvalues are the diagonal entries themselves: 3 and 5. Their sum (trace) = 3+5 = 8.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Correct answer is the sum (trace), not the product (which is 15).
(B) This is the product (det), not the sum, of the eigenvalues.
(C) Not obtained from any correct combination of the eigenvalues.
(D) Not obtained from any correct combination of the eigenvalues.

questions.question: The differential equation d²y/dx² + 4y = 0 is classified as:
questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• The highest derivative present is d²y/dx² (second order); y and its derivatives appear only to the first power with constant coefficients (linear); and the right-hand side is zero (homogeneous).
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Incorrect order — the equation involves a second derivative.
(B) Correct.
(C) The equation is linear, not nonlinear (y and y'' appear only to first power).
(D) Incorrect on both order and linearity classification.

questions.question: A random variable X takes the values 2, 4, 6, each with equal probability 1/3. Compute the variance of X.
questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• Mean = (2+4+6)/3 = 4.
• Variance = [(2−4)²+(4−4)²+(6−4)²]/3 = (4+0+4)/3 = 8/3 = 2.67.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Not obtained from the correct sum of squared deviations.
(B) Correct.
(C) Not obtained from the correct sum of squared deviations divided by 3.
(D) Equals the mean, not the variance — a common confusion.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫₀² (2x + 1) dx.
questions.solution:
Answer: 5.90 to 6.10
Explanation:
• ∫(2x+1)dx = x² + x, evaluated from 0 to 2 = (4+2) − 0 = 6.

questions.question: In a combine harvester, the primary function of the "concave" (positioned below the threshing cylinder) is to:

options.A: Separate straw from grain after threshing
options.B: Thresh grain from the head by rubbing/impact action against the rotating cylinder
options.C: Clean chaff from the grain using an air blast
options.D: Convey threshed grain to the grain tank

questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• The concave works together with the threshing cylinder: grain heads are rubbed and impacted between the rotating cylinder and the stationary concave, separating grain from the head.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) This is the function of the straw walkers, not the concave.
(B) Correct.
(C) This is the function of the cleaning shoe/fan, not the concave.
(D) This is the function of the grain auger/elevator, not the concave.

questions.question: A roller-chain drive has a driving sprocket with 20 teeth running at 300 rpm and a driven sprocket with 12 teeth. Find the driven sprocket speed.
questions.solution:
Answer: C
Explanation:
• N₁T₁ = N₂T₂ ⟹ N₂ = N₁T₁/T₂ = (300×20)/12 = 500 rpm.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Results from inverting the teeth ratio.
(B) This is the driving sprocket speed itself, not the driven speed.
(C) Correct.
(D) Not consistent with the correct teeth ratio.

questions.question: A thresher processes paddy at 800 kg/h total input, with a straw-to-grain mass ratio of 1.5:1. Compute the grain output rate.
questions.solution:
Answer: 315.00 to 325.00 kg/h
Explanation:
• Total input = straw + grain = 1.5×grain + grain = 2.5×grain.
• Grain = 800/2.5 = 320 kg/h.

questions.question: A standardized Tractor Test (e.g. as conducted at a national test station) primarily evaluates:

options.A: Operator seat cushioning and cabin paint quality only
options.B: Engine power, fuel consumption, and drawbar performance under standardized conditions

questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• Standardized tractor tests measure engineering performance — PTO/engine power, specific fuel consumption, and drawbar pull-vs-speed characteristics — under controlled, repeatable conditions.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Not the purpose of a standardized performance test.
(B) Correct.
(C) Not the purpose of a standardized performance test.
(D) Resale value is a market outcome, not a tested engineering parameter.

questions.question: Wheel slip of a tractor drive wheel is defined as:
questions.solution:
Answer: A
Explanation:
• Slip is the fractional shortfall of actual travel distance relative to the theoretical (no-slip) distance computed from wheel revolutions, expressed as a percentage.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Correct.
(B) This gives (1−slip fraction)×100, not slip itself.
(C) Uses the wrong reference (actual) denominator and wrong sign convention.
(D) Not a standard definition of slip.

questions.question: A 4-cylinder, 4-stroke engine has a total swept volume of 2400 cm³ (equal among cylinders) and a clearance volume of 50 cm³ per cylinder. Compute the compression ratio.
questions.solution:
Answer: 12.80 to 13.20
Explanation:
• Swept volume per cylinder = 2400/4 = 600 cm³.
• Compression ratio = (Vs+Vc)/Vc = (600+50)/50 = 650/50 = 13.0.

questions.question: In a PTO performance test, a tractor delivers 45 kW at the PTO shaft against a rated engine power of 52 kW. Compute the PTO transmission efficiency.
questions.solution:
Answer: 86.00 to 87.00 %
Explanation:
• Transmission efficiency = (PTO power/Engine power) × 100 = (45/52) × 100 = 86.5%.

questions.question: The primary purpose of a loose/brushwood "gully plug" (temporary check structure) in watershed management is to:

options.A: Increase the peak discharge passing through the gully
options.B: Reduce runoff velocity and trap sediment within small, active gullies
options.C: Divert water exclusively for irrigation use

questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• A gully plug is a low-cost temporary structure placed across small gullies to slow flow velocity, promote sediment deposition, and arrest gully head-cutting/widening.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Contradicts the intended function — gully plugs reduce, not increase, effective peak velocity/discharge locally.
(B) Correct.
(C) Diversion for irrigation is not the function of a gully plug.
(D) Streamflow measurement is done by gauging structures (e.g. weirs), not gully plugs.

questions.question: For fully developed laminar flow in a circular pipe, the Darcy friction factor f is given by:
questions.solution:
Answer: A
Explanation:
• For laminar flow (Re < 2000), the Darcy friction factor follows the exact analytical result f = 64/Re, derived from the Hagen–Poiseuille solution.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Correct.
(B) This is the Blasius correlation for turbulent flow, not laminar flow.
(C) This is the Fanning (not Darcy) friction factor expression for laminar flow.
(D) This is a turbulent-flow correlation (related to Blasius), not applicable to laminar flow.

questions.question: Using USLE with R = 420 MJ·mm/(ha·h·yr), K = 0.28, LS = 2.1, C = 0.20, and P = 0.6, compute the annual soil loss A.
In a levelling survey, a back sight of 1.865 m is taken on a benchmark of RL 250.000 m, followed by a fore sight of 2.340 m on the next point. Find the RL of that point.
questions.solution:
Answer: 249.45 to 249.60 m
Explanation:
• Height of instrument = 250.000 + 1.865 = 251.865 m.
• RL of next point = 251.865 − 2.340 = 249.525 m.

questions.question: "Field capacity" is defined as the soil moisture content:

options.A: At which plants permanently wilt and cannot recover
options.B: Retained by the soil after gravitational drainage has essentially ceased, roughly 1–3 days after saturation
options.D: At full saturation, with all pore space filled with water

questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• Field capacity is the water content held against gravity in the soil profile after free drainage has largely stopped — the upper limit of plant-available water.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) This describes permanent wilting point, not field capacity.
(B) Correct.
(C) This describes oven-dry (0% moisture) condition, not field capacity.
(D) This describes saturation, a wetter condition than field capacity.

questions.question: An unconfined aquifer has average transmissivity T = 380 m²/day and hydraulic conductivity K = 19 m/day. Find the average saturated thickness.
questions.solution:
Answer: 19.50 to 20.50 m
Explanation:
• T = K×b ⟹ b = T/K = 380/19 = 20 m.

questions.question: In rice milling, the operation that removes the husk from paddy without removing the bran layer is called:
questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• Dehusking (shelling) separates the outer husk from paddy to yield brown rice, leaving the bran layer intact; whitening/polishing are later steps that remove the bran.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Polishing removes bran/germ residue after whitening — a later step, not husk removal.
(B) Correct.
(C) Whitening removes the bran layer — it comes after dehusking, not instead of it.
(D) Grading sorts milled rice by size, unrelated to husk removal.

questions.question: The terminal velocity of a grain kernel in an air stream is primarily used to design:
questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• Terminal velocity governs the air velocity needed to convey grain pneumatically or to separate lighter chaff/dust from heavier grain in an aspirator — both aerodynamic separation/conveying applications.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Bin wall slope is set from angle of repose, not terminal velocity.
(B) Correct.
(C) Roller gap is set from kernel size/hardness, not terminal velocity.
(D) Floor slope is a structural/handling detail, not set by terminal velocity.

questions.question: Using Rittinger's law, reducing a material from 10 mm to 4 mm requires 8 kJ/kg. Find the energy required to further reduce it from 4 mm to 2 mm.
1500 kg of grain at 20% moisture content (wb) is dried to 14% (wb). Compute the mass of water removed.
questions.solution:
Answer: 103.00 to 107.00 kg
Explanation:
• Dry matter (constant) = 1500×(1−0.20) = 1200 kg.
• Final wet mass = 1200/(1−0.14) = 1200/0.86 = 1395.3 kg.
• Water removed = 1500 − 1395.3 = 104.7 kg.

questions.question: Tomato juice is concentrated from 5% total solids (TS) to 28% TS in a single-effect evaporator. For a feed rate of 3000 kg/h, compute the water evaporated per hour.
questions.solution:
Answer: 2440.00 to 2490.00 kg/h
Explanation:
• Solids in feed (constant) = 3000×0.05 = 150 kg/h.
• Concentrated product mass = 150/0.28 = 535.7 kg/h.
• Water evaporated = 3000 − 535.7 = 2464.3 kg/h.

questions.topic: Unit Operations in Dairy & Food Engineering (rotation
questions.question: Homogenization of milk primarily achieves:

options.B: Reduction and uniform distribution of fat globule size, preventing creaming/separation
options.C: Removal of water to concentrate total solids

questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• Homogenization mechanically breaks down fat globules to a small, uniform size so they remain dispersed rather than rising to form a cream layer.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) This is the function of pasteurization, not homogenization.
(B) This describes evaporation/concentration, not homogenization.
(C) Unrelated to homogenization; relevant to certain dairy crystallization processes instead.
(D) Correct.

questions.question: A plate heat exchanger has overall heat transfer coefficient U = 2200 W/m²K, area 4.0 m², and LMTD 10°C. Compute the heat transfer rate.
questions.solution:
Answer: 87.00 to 89.00 kW
Explanation:
• Q = U×A×LMTD = 2200×4.0×10 = 88,000 W = 88 kW.

questions.question: For the matrix A = [[4, 2], [1, 3]], compute det(A).
questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• det(A) = (4×3) − (2×1) = 12 − 2 = 10.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Results from omitting the subtraction of the off-diagonal product.
(B) Correct.
(C) This is the product of the diagonal entries only (before subtracting).
(D) Not obtained from a correct 2×2 determinant calculation.

questions.question: Using the Newton–Raphson method to find a root of f(x) = x² − 5, starting from x₀ = 2, compute x₁ after one iteration.
questions.solution:
Answer: C
Explanation:
• Newton–Raphson: x₁ = x₀ − f(x₀)/f'(x₀), with f(x)=x²−5, f'(x)=2x.
• f(2) = 4−5 = −1; f'(2) = 4.
• x₁ = 2 − (−1/4) = 2 + 0.25 = 2.25.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) This is x₀ itself, before any iteration.
(B) Not obtained from the correct Newton–Raphson update.
(C) Correct.
(D) Overshoots — not consistent with the correct update formula.

questions.question: Solve dy/dx = 3x², with y(1) = 2. Find y(2).
questions.solution:
Answer: 8.90 to 9.10
Explanation:
• Integrating: y = x³ + C.
• At x=1, y=2 ⟹ C = 2−1 = 1, so y = x³+1.
• At x=2: y(2) = 8+1 = 9.

questions.question: Using the trapezoidal rule with 2 equal intervals, estimate ∫₀² x² dx.
questions.solution:
Answer: 2.90 to 3.10
Explanation:
• h = 1; nodes x₀=0, x₁=1, x₂=2; f(x)=x² gives f₀=0, f₁=1, f₂=4.
• Trapezoidal estimate = (h/2)[f₀ + 2f₁ + f₂] = (1/2)[0+2+4] = 3.0.
• (The exact value is 8/3 ≈ 2.667; the trapezoidal rule overestimates for a convex function.)

questions.question: A combine harvester threshing cylinder has a diameter of 600 mm and rotates at 700 rpm. Recommended rasp-bar peripheral speed for paddy threshing is 20–25 m/s. Compute the peripheral speed and state whether it falls within the recommended range.
questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• Peripheral speed v = πDN/60 = π×0.6×700/60 = π×7 = 22.0 m/s.
• 22.0 m/s lies within the recommended 20–25 m/s band for paddy.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Not obtained from the correct πDN/60 calculation.
(B) Correct.
(C) Not obtained from the correct calculation at the given D and N.
(D) Not obtained from the correct calculation at the given D and N.

questions.question: A shaft transmits 25 kW at 400 rpm. Compute the torque transmitted.

A combine harvester costs ₹25,00,000, has a life of 8 years, and a salvage value of 12% of the purchase price. Using straight-line depreciation, and given an annual repair-and-maintenance cost of 5% of the purchase price, compute the total annual fixed-plus-repair cost (excluding fuel and labour).
A chisel plough with 7 shanks operates at 250 mm depth; each shank has an effective working width of 300 mm, and the soil's specific draft resistance is 45 kN/m². Compute the total draft force.
questions.solution:
Answer: 23.30 to 23.90 kN
Explanation:
• Cross-section per shank = 0.25×0.30 = 0.075 m².
• Total cross-section (7 shanks) = 7×0.075 = 0.525 m².
• Draft = 0.525×45 = 23.625 kN.

questions.question: An air-standard Diesel cycle has a compression ratio of 16 and a cut-off ratio of 2.0. Taking γ = 1.4, compute the thermal efficiency.
questions.solution:
Answer: C
Explanation:
• η = 1 − [1/r^(γ−1)] × [(ρ^γ − 1)/(γ(ρ−1))], r=16, ρ=2.0, γ=1.4.
• r^(γ−1) = 16^0.4 = 3.032.
• ρ^γ = 2^1.4 = 2.639; (ρ^γ−1) = 1.639; γ(ρ−1) = 1.4×1 = 1.4; bracket = 1.639/1.4 = 1.171.
• η = 1 − (1/3.032)×1.171 = 1 − 0.386 = 0.614 = 61.4%.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Not consistent with the correct Diesel-cycle efficiency formula at r=16, ρ=2.0.
(B) Not consistent with the correct calculation.
(C) Correct.
(D) Overestimates — exceeds what these values yield.

questions.question: A 4WD tractor weighs 22 kN, with static weight distribution 55% front / 45% rear. During pulling, weight transfer shifts 2 kN from the front axle to the rear axle. The effective coefficient of traction (all-wheel-drive, based on total dynamic weight) is 0.6, and the overall rolling resistance coefficient is 0.07. Compute the maximum drawbar pull.
questions.solution:
Answer: 11.50 to 11.90 kN
Explanation:
• Since all wheels are driven, maximum tractive force is governed by total weight: F_t(max) = 0.6 × 22 = 13.2 kN.
• Total rolling resistance = 0.07 × 22 = 1.54 kN.
• Maximum drawbar pull = 13.2 − 1.54 = 11.66 kN.

questions.question: A tractor diesel engine has a brake specific fuel consumption of 210 g/kWh; the calorific value of the diesel used is 42.5 MJ/kg. Compute the brake thermal efficiency.

A tractor gearbox output shaft runs at 900 rpm and delivers 35 kW into a final-drive-plus-differential assembly with an overall reduction ratio of 18:1 and combined mechanical efficiency of 94%. Compute the torque delivered at the wheel axle.
questions.solution:
Answer: 6200.00 to 6380.00 N·m
Explanation:
• Wheel axle speed = 900/18 = 50 rpm = 50×2π/60 = 5.236 rad/s.
• Power delivered at the axle = 35 × 0.94 = 32.9 kW.
• Torque = Power/ω = 32,900/5.236 = 6284 N·m.

questions.question: A wind-powered water pump has a rotor swept area of 4 m², operates at a wind speed of 6 m/s, and has an overall wind-to-water power conversion efficiency of 25%. Taking air density = 1.2 kg/m³, compute the power delivered to the water.
questions.solution:
Answer: 126.00 to 134.00 W
Explanation:
• Available wind power = 0.5×ρ×A×v³ = 0.5×1.2×4×6³ = 0.5×1.2×4×216 = 518.4 W.
• Delivered power = 518.4 × 0.25 = 129.6 W.

questions.question: A small watershed of area 8 km² has a runoff coefficient of 0.35 for a design rainfall intensity of 40 mm/h. Using the Rational Method, Q = CiA/360 (Q in m³/s, i in mm/h, A in hectares), compute the peak discharge.
questions.solution:
Answer: C
Explanation:
• A = 8 km² = 800 ha.
• Q = (0.35×40×800)/360 = 11,200/360 = 31.1 m³/s.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Not consistent with the correct substitution into the Rational formula.
(B) Not consistent with the correct substitution.
(C) Correct.
(D) Overestimates — does not match the correct Rational-method calculation.

questions.question: A 6-hour unit hydrograph (1 cm rainfall excess) has a peak discharge of 60 m³/s. For a storm producing a uniform rainfall excess of 2.5 cm in 6 hours, neglecting baseflow, compute the peak of the direct-runoff hydrograph.
questions.solution:
Answer: B
Explanation:
• Unit hydrograph ordinates scale linearly with rainfall excess depth: Peak of DRH = 60 × 2.5 = 150 m³/s.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Not consistent with correct linear scaling by 2.5.
(B) Correct.
(C) Not consistent with correct linear scaling.
(D) Results from dividing instead of multiplying by 2.5.

questions.question: A trapezoidal (Cipolletti) check-dam spillway must pass a peak discharge of 3.5 m³/s. Using Q = 1.71 L H^1.5 (SI units), with an available head H = 0.5 m, find the minimum crest length L.

Water flows through a 200 mm diameter pipe at a mean velocity of 1.8 m/s and discharges into a trapezoidal open channel with bed width 1.0 m, side slopes 1:1, flowing at a depth of 0.6 m. Using continuity, compute the mean velocity in the channel.
questions.solution:
Answer: 0.06 to 0.06 m/s
Explanation:
• Pipe discharge Q = (π/4)×0.2²×1.8 = 0.03142×1.8 = 0.0566 m³/s.
• Channel area = (1.0+0.6)×0.6 = 0.96 m².
• Channel velocity = 0.0566/0.96 = 0.0589 m/s.

questions.question: A watershed has curve number CN = 78. For a rainfall event of 75 mm, using the SCS-CN method (S = 25400/CN − 254, Ia = 0.2S), compute the direct runoff depth Q.
A soil has field capacity 30% and permanent wilting point 14% (both by dry weight), and bulk density 1.35 g/cm³. Compute the total available water in a 45 cm effective root-zone depth.
questions.solution:
Answer: 96.00 to 98.50 mm
Explanation:
• Available water fraction = 0.30 − 0.14 = 0.16.
• Depth of available water = 0.16 × 1.35 × 450 mm = 97.2 mm.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about specific speed (Nₛ) and centrifugal-pump selection are CORRECT?

options.A: Low specific speed corresponds to radial-flow (centrifugal) pumps, suited to high head and low discharge
options.B: High specific speed corresponds to axial-flow (propeller) pumps, suited to low head and high discharge
options.C: Specific speed depends only on discharge and is independent of head and rotational speed
options.D: Mixed-flow pumps have specific speed values intermediate between radial- and axial-flow types

questions.solution:
Answer: A, B, D
Explanation:
• A, B and D correctly describe how specific speed classifies pump geometry.
• C is false — specific speed is a function of rotational speed N, discharge Q, AND head H (Nₛ = N√Q/H^0.75), not discharge alone.
Option-wise justification:
(A) Correct — the standard low-Ns/radial-flow association.
(B) Correct — the standard high-Ns/axial-flow association.
(C) Incorrect — specific speed depends on N, Q and H together, not Q alone.
(D) Correct — mixed-flow pumps occupy the intermediate Ns range.

questions.question: A lined trapezoidal channel has bed width 1.5 m, side slopes 1.5:1 (H:V), depth of flow 1.0 m, bed slope 1 in 2500, and Manning's n = 0.016. Compute the discharge.
Design a subsurface drain spacing using the steady-state Hooghoudt equation q·S² = 4K·h·(2d+h), with K = 0.6 m/day, h = 1.0 m, d = 1.5 m, and q = 0.012 m/day. Compute the drain spacing S.

A steady-state pumping test on a confined aquifer (Q = 1500 m³/day) records drawdown of 1.8 m at radial distance 15 m and 0.7 m at radial distance 90 m. Using the Thiem equation, compute the transmissivity T.
Which of the following statements about controlled-atmosphere (CA) storage of fresh produce are CORRECT?

options.A: CA storage typically maintains reduced O₂ and elevated CO₂ levels compared to normal air
options.B: CA storage slows the respiration rate and senescence of produce, extending storage life
options.C: CA storage increases ethylene production, accelerating ripening
options.D: Optimal O₂/CO₂ levels for CA storage are commodity-specific

questions.solution:
Answer: A, B, D
Explanation:
• A, B and D correctly describe CA storage principles and practice.
• C is false — CA storage is used to SUPPRESS ethylene-driven ripening/senescence, not accelerate it.
Option-wise justification:
(A) Correct — the defining feature of CA storage.
(B) Correct — the central benefit of CA storage.
(C) Incorrect — CA storage reduces, not increases, ethylene-driven ripening.
(D) Correct — optimal gas composition varies by commodity and cultivar.

questions.question: Maize at 24% moisture content (wb) is dried at a constant rate Rc = 0.035 kg water/kg dry matter/h until the critical moisture content of 15% (wb) is reached. Compute the time taken during the constant-rate period.
questions.solution:
Answer: 3.85 to 4.10 h
Explanation:
• Convert wb to db: M(db) = M(wb)/(1−M(wb)).
• Initial: 0.24/0.76 = 0.3158 kg water/kg dry matter.
• Critical: 0.15/0.85 = 0.1765 kg water/kg dry matter.
• Moisture removed (db) = 0.3158 − 0.1765 = 0.1393 kg water/kg dry matter.
• Time = 0.1393/0.035 = 3.98 h.

questions.question: A roller mill grinds wheat at 800 kg/h from a feed size of 6 mm to a product size of 1.5 mm. Using Bond's law, E(kWh/tonne) = Wi(1/√Dp2 − 1/√Dp1) with Bond work index Wi = 10.2 kWh/tonne and Dp in mm, compute the power required.
A silo holds 400 tonnes of maize at 16% moisture content (wb) and must be dried to 13% (wb) for safe long-term storage. Using a dry-matter balance, compute the mass of water to be removed.
questions.solution:
Answer: 13.40 to 14.20 tonnes
Explanation:
• Dry matter (constant) = 400×(1−0.16) = 336 t.
• Final wet mass = 336/(1−0.13) = 336/0.87 = 386.2 t.
• Water removed = 400 − 386.2 = 13.8 t.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the F₀ value (thermal process lethality) used in canned-food sterilization are CORRECT?

options.A: F₀ is the equivalent time at a reference temperature (usually 121.1°C) that delivers the same microbial lethality as the actual, varying time-temperature process
options.B: A higher F₀ indicates a more severe (more lethal) thermal process
options.C: F₀ depends on the Z-value of the target organism
options.D: F₀ is independent of the retort's come-up and cool-down time

questions.solution:
Answer: A, B, C
Explanation:
• A, B and C correctly describe F₀ and its dependence on the organism's Z-value.
• D is false — accumulated lethality during the heating (come-up) and cooling phases of the retort cycle contributes to F₀ and must be included, not ignored.
Option-wise justification:
(A) Correct — the standard definition of F₀.
(B) Correct — F₀ scales with process severity.
(C) Correct — F₀ is organism-specific through the Z-value.
(D) Incorrect — come-up and cool-down lethality contribute to F₀ and cannot be neglected.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about membrane processing (ultrafiltration/reverse osmosis) in dairy processing are CORRECT?

options.A: Ultrafiltration separates components primarily based on molecular size using a semi-permeable membrane
options.B: Reverse osmosis requires a higher applied pressure than ultrafiltration for a comparable flux
options.C: Ultrafiltration can concentrate milk proteins while allowing lactose and water to pass through as permeate
options.D: Membrane fouling has no effect on permeate flux over the course of operation

questions.solution:
Answer: A, B, C
Explanation:
• A, B and C correctly describe UF/RO membrane separation principles applied to milk.
• D is false — fouling progressively reduces permeate flux over time and is a major practical limitation of membrane processing.
Option-wise justification:
(A) Correct — the defining separation mechanism of UF.
(B) Correct — RO membranes have smaller pore size and need higher driving pressure than UF.
(C) Correct — this is the basis of milk protein concentration by UF.
(D) Incorrect — fouling reduces flux progressively; it is not negligible.
